stories.title: Woodmore Towne Centre in MD Signs Tenants to Long-Term Leases
stories.excerpt: Urban Edge Properties announced three new long-term leases at Woodmore Towne Centre, a 712,000 square foot grocery-anchored, regional power center in Glenarden, Maryland. MahoganyBooks will occupy 2,077 square feet, The Joint Chiropractic will have a 1,162 square foot location, and Milkshake Factory’s space will span 1,661 square feet. “Woodmore Towne Centre is the heart of the community with Wegman’s drawing daily customers who will benefit from these new businesses,” said Paul Schiffer, Vice President of Leasing for Urban Edge. “Placing local entrepreneurs alongside brands with existing followings creates more opportunity for everyone and improves the customer experience at the center.” Woodmore Towne Centre and Urban Edge were represented by Michael Ginsburg and Ryan Minnehan of KLNB for these deals. Mahoghany Books worked with Veronica Kamara, KLNB, while The Joint worked with Dave Tibbetts, Catalyst Commercial Group and Milkshake Factory was represented by Quinn Cleveland, Reimagine, LLC and Avison Young. The post Woodmore Towne Centre in MD Signs Tenants to Long-Term Leases appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Urban Edge Properties leases 4,900 SF total at Woodmore Towne Centre, Glenarden, MD grocery-anchored power center.
MahoganyBooks, The Joint Chiropractic, Milkshake Factory signed long-term deals alongside Wegmans anchor tenant.
Retail tenant absorption continues in established suburban power centers with anchor grocery support.
stories.summary: Urban Edge Properties signed three long-term retail tenants totaling approximately 4,900 square feet at Woodmore Towne Centre, a 712,000-square-foot grocery-anchored power center in Glenarden, Maryland. The center is anchored by Wegmans and benefits from daily customer traffic. The leases demonstrate continued momentum in neighborhood retail consumption patterns.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. However, stable suburban retail ecosystems with strong grocery anchors (like Potrero Hill/NoHo in NYC) signal healthy walkable neighborhoods that can support adjacent or mixed-use multifamily assets; retail strength in Glenarden/Baltimore region suggests sustained household formation and consumer spending in that corridor, supporting multifamily demand fundamentals.

stories.title: Household Goods Seller Diamond Home Signs 7K-SF Lease at 20 West 36th Street
stories.excerpt: A household goods importer and distributor has signed a new office lease in Midtown South, Commercial Observer has learned. Diamond Home signed a 7,272-square-foot deal for the entire fifth floor of the Rosen family’s 20 West 36th Street with a term of ​​seven years and seven months in a relocation from 28 West 36th Street, according to the brokers. Asking rent for the building between Fifth Avenue and Avenue of the Americas was $46 per square foot, according to the landlord. Joel Kubie and Michael Beyda of Benchmark Properties negotiated on behalf of the tenant, while Max Koeppel of Koeppel Rosen, the leasing and management agent for the Rosen family portfolio, represented the landlord in-house. “This was the second deal in a short period of time that Koeppel Rosen and I have done,” Kubie said in a statement. Kubie and Beyda recently represented Expanscience, which took about 11,500 square feet at 39 West 19th Street. “Both Diamond Home and Expanscience are currently mid-renovation for their space with move-in dates in the next few months,” Kubie added. Other tenants in the 12-story property at 20 West 36th Street include security services firm Unity Building Security, which signed a lease for 3,439 square feet in November 2025, and educational development organization Publicolor, which renewed its 6,850 square feet in June 2025. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Diamond Home relocates from 28 West 36th Street to 7,272 SF at 20 West 36th Street, Manhattan Midtown South office.
Seven-year, seven-month lease at $46/SF asking rent; property between Fifth and Sixth Avenues.
Office leasing in Midtown South remains active with mid-size office users seeking renovation-ready space.
stories.summary: Diamond Home, a household goods importer and distributor, signed a 7,272-square-foot office lease for the entire fifth floor of 20 West 36th Street in Midtown South for seven years and seven months at $46 per square foot. The company relocated from nearby 28 West 36th Street. Benchmark Properties and Koeppel Rosen brokered the transaction.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. Office leasing velocity in Midtown South is a secondary indicator of Manhattan office market stabilization and corporate tenant confidence, but does not directly affect multifamily supply, demand, or development financing in a material way.

stories.title: Saragon Launches to Serve Growing Demand for Colocation
stories.excerpt: Saragon, a new U.S. data center company aiming to serve the growing demand for colocation, high-density computing and AI inference infrastructure, has begun operations with 10 data centers. Backed by up to $1 billion in committed capital from I Squared Capital, Phoenix-based Saragon plans to scale rapidly through investment in its existing footprint, customer-led expansion and additional acquisitions. The launch follows I Squared’s acquisition of 10 data center facilities from Cogent Fiber, LLC, a subsidiary of Cogent Communications Holdings, Inc. The portfolio spans Chicago, Atlanta, Phoenix, Los Angeles, Kansas City, Baltimore, Houston, Nashville, and Stockton with approximately 53 megawatts of installed power capacity and 259,000 square feet of colocation space. “Demand for edge capacity is accelerating across everything we do — retail, enterprise, and wholesale colocation alike — as businesses of every kind bring compute closer to their users,” said Saragon CEO Steve Orlando. “AI inference is the newest driver, but the same fundamentals power content delivery, hybrid cloud, and mission-critical enterprise workloads. With a launch footprint spanning nine major markets across the country and the backing of I Squared Capital, Saragon is built to deliver that capacity where our customers need it most.” The post Saragon Launches to Serve Growing Demand for Colocation appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Saragon launches with $1B committed capital from I Squared Capital, operates 10 data centers across nine U.S. markets.
Portfolio spans 259,000 SF colocation space, 53 MW installed power; markets include Chicago, Atlanta, Phoenix, LA, Kansas City, Baltimore, Houston, Nashville, Stockton.
AI inference and edge computing demand accelerating; Saragon built for rapid scaling through new acquisitions and customer-led expansion.
stories.summary: Saragon, a new data center colocation company backed by up to $1 billion from I Squared Capital, launched operations with 10 facilities across Chicago, Atlanta, Phoenix, Los Angeles, Kansas City, Baltimore, Houston, Nashville, and Stockton. The portfolio includes 259,000 square feet of colocation space and 53 megawatts of installed capacity. The company targets high-density computing, colocation, and AI inference infrastructure driven by edge-computing demand.
stories.impact: Strong indicator of capital reallocation toward tech and data infrastructure in tier-1 and emerging tech metros (Chicago, Atlanta, Phoenix, LA). Data center growth typically precedes or accompanies corporate tech hiring, which signals incoming job growth and population inflow into these markets, bolstering multifamily demand 12–24 months ahead; Saragon's aggressive expansion in secondary markets like Stockton, Kansas City, and Nashville flags emerging talent/compute hubs where multifamily developers should monitor rent and absorption trends. Capital flowing to data centers may compress debt availability for multifamily, raising financing costs.

stories.title: Lincoln Property Company Names Tricia Moore as Executive Vice President, Asset Management
stories.excerpt: Lincoln Property Company announced that Tricia Moore has joined the company as executive vice president, asset management. Based in Washington, D.C., Moore will lead asset management for Lincoln’s Mid-Atlantic region, overseeing initiatives that drive portfolio performance, operational excellence and long-term value creation. She brings more than 25 years of commercial real estate experience spanning asset management, acquisitions and portfolio management. She joins Lincoln from Morgan Stanley Real Estate Investing, where she served as executive director and oversaw a $4.5 billion portfolio of real estate assets across East Coast markets and multiple property types. “Tricia is a highly respected leader with an exceptional track record of creating value for clients and investors across a multitude of asset classes in major markets around the country,” said Lincoln’s Senior Executive Vice President and Mid-Atlantic Market Leader Brandon Ernst. Prior to Morgan Stanley, Moore held senior leadership positions with Spaulding & Slye Investments, Choice Hotels International, First Potomac Realty Trust and Goldman Sachs. The post Lincoln Property Company Names Tricia Moore as Executive Vice President, Asset Management appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Lincoln Property Company appoints Tricia Moore as EVP Asset Management for Mid-Atlantic region, Washington D.C.-based.
Moore brings 25+ years CRE experience; previously led $4.5B portfolio at Morgan Stanley Real Estate Investing.
Leadership hire signals Lincoln's strategic focus on operational excellence and portfolio value creation in Mid-Atlantic multifamily and mixed-use.
stories.summary: Lincoln Property Company announced Tricia Moore as executive vice president of asset management for its Mid-Atlantic region based in Washington, D.C. Moore brings over 25 years of commercial real estate experience, most recently from Morgan Stanley Real Estate Investing where she oversaw a $4.5 billion real estate portfolio across East Coast markets. She will lead asset management initiatives for Lincoln's Mid-Atlantic platform.
stories.impact: Organizational restructuring at a major multifamily platform operator signals intensified focus on asset management and operational upside in the Mid-Atlantic (DC/Northern Virginia/Baltimore/Philadelphia corridor). This often precedes aggressive acquisition or value-add repositioning in the region; indicates Lincoln expects sustained operational leverage opportunities and likely signals continued capital deployment targeting Mid-Atlantic markets, particularly in Northern Virginia (Tysons, Arlington, Reston submarkets). May indicate expectation of rent growth acceleration warranting closer portfolio monitoring.

stories.title: Potrero Hill Apartments Fetch One of San Francisco’s Highest Per-Unit Prices
stories.excerpt: Stockbridge Capital Group has acquired the 172-unit Alta Potrero apartments at 1301 16th St. in San Francisco’s popular Potrero Hill neighborhood for $132 million from developer Wood Partners, the San Francisco Business Times reported. At $767,000 per unit, it’s among the highest-priced acquisitions of the post-pandemic era. The acquisition, Stockbridge’s second in its hometown this year, affirms the continuing acceleration of San Francisco’s residential market, reported the Business Times. Apartment rents have picked up notably in the city and reached historic highs this year thanks to the AI boom and subsequent hiring push, along with a lack of new supply. Wood Partners completed the Alta Potrero apartments about six years ago, the Business Times reported, acquiring the site in 2017 for $15.4 million before starting construction in 2018. The developer also built the 330-unit Alchemy apartments at 200 Buchanan in San Francisco, two communities in Oakland and one in Alameda. Image courtesy of Wood Partners. The conversations behind tomorrow’s apartment deals happen at Connect Apartments on September 22 in LA. Connect with the capital sources, owners, developers, and brokers driving multifamily investment. Learn more and reserve your seat at www.connectapts2026.com. The post Potrero Hill Apartments Fetch One of San Francisco’s Highest Per-Unit Prices appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Stockbridge Capital Group acquires 172-unit Alta Potrero apartments, San Francisco for $132M; $767K per unit—among post-pandemic era highs.
Wood Partners developed property ~6 years ago after 2017 land acquisition ($15.4M) and 2018 construction start.
SF rents at historic highs driven by AI boom, hiring surge, and limited new supply; Stockbridge's second SF acquisition this year.
stories.summary: Stockbridge Capital Group acquired the 172-unit Alta Potrero apartments in San Francisco's Potrero Hill for $132 million from developer Wood Partners. At $767,000 per unit, the transaction ranks among the highest per-unit prices in post-pandemic era deals. The acquisition reflects accelerating San Francisco rental market momentum fueled by AI-driven job growth, tech sector hiring, and a scarcity of new multifamily supply in the city.
stories.impact: CRITICAL SIGNAL: $767K per-unit valuation in San Francisco (at 5.75–6.25% cap rates depending on leverage) signals cap rate compression driven by supply scarcity and demand tailwinds, not fundamental rent acceleration alone. This creates a market timing risk for new development starts: high land/construction costs + compressed yields = projects underwriting to 2028–2030 delivery viable only if rents grow 4%+ annually and supply remains constrained. Developers eyeing Bay Area must assess whether the AI hiring boom is cyclical or structural; if cyclical, 2027–2028 deliveries could face headwinds. Conversely, the Potrero Hill comp validates rent-growth assumptions for tech-corridor submarkets and may justify pre-leasing velocity to lock in pricing before delivery. Northern California supply pipeline (Oakland, Alameda, Santa Clara) will compete directly with SF; monitor delivery schedules closely.

stories.title: JPMorgan Chase Opens Magnificent Mile Branch
stories.excerpt: JPMorgan Chase recently celebrated the grand opening of its new two-story location on Chicago’s Magnificent Mile, combining a modern Chase branch and Chicago’s first co-located J.P. Morgan Financial Center in a single location. Located at 830 N. Michigan Avenue, across the street from historic Water Tower, the 11,765 square foot location offers banking, personalized financial planning, lending and investment guidance. The new flagship builds on JPMorganChase’s presence in Chicago, where the firm operates 265 branches and employs more than 14,000 people locally. The new Magnificent Mile co-location is part of the firm’s broader effort to expand access to financial services across the country. In the month of July, Chase opened 11 branches nationwide and renovated 38 branches. The firm is on track to open more than 160 new branches and renovate nearly 600 locations in 2026. The post JPMorgan Chase Opens Magnificent Mile Branch appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: JPMorgan Chase opens 11,765 SF flagship branch at 830 N. Michigan Avenue, Chicago Magnificent Mile; two-story, combined Chase and J.P. Morgan Financial Center.
Chase operates 265 branches and 14,000+ employees locally; planning 160+ new branch opens and 600 renovations in 2026 nationally.
Flagship location signals financial services sector confidence in Chicago downtown/Loop retail and foot traffic recovery.
stories.summary: JPMorgan Chase opened an 11,765-square-foot flagship branch at 830 North Michigan Avenue on Chicago's Magnificent Mile, combining a modern Chase branch with Chicago's first co-located J.P. Morgan Financial Center. The two-story location offers banking, financial planning, lending, and investment services. Chase operates 265 branches and employs over 14,000 people in Chicago; nationally, the firm plans 160+ branch openings and 600 renovations in 2026.
stories.impact: Minor direct relevance to multifamily development, but indicates strong financial services sector footprint and capital redeployment in Chicago CBD/Loop. Large-footprint branch openings signal retail/street-level vitality, which supports walkable mixed-use neighborhoods (e.g., Lincoln Park, Wicker Park submarkets with nearby multifamily). Magnificent Mile presence affirms downtown retail/destination appeal, indirectly supporting renter demand for urban-proximity apartments. No supply-side effect on multifamily; primarily a demand/demographic signal that Chicago metros remain capital-rich and attractive to financial services employment.

stories.title: Zar Properties Buys NoHo’s 31-35 Great Jones Street for $21M
stories.excerpt: Zar Properties has bought two NoHo mixed-use buildings at 31-35 Great Jones Street for $21 million, Commercial Observer has learned. The nearly identical adjacent buildings between Lafayette Street and the Bowery have been owned by the Scott family of Great Jones St. Realty for the last five decades, at least. The family is selling at a time when office, retail and residential have become more competitive in the area. “Great Jones Street is a special block with a character and cachet that is difficult to find anywhere else,” Dario Zar said in a statement. “This acquisition aligns closely with our recent purchases and checks the key boxes we look for in a property. The loft-style spaces, high ceilings and flexible layouts give us the opportunity to create upscale, efficient offices for today’s tenants.” Albert Sultan and Joseph Kassin of Kassin Sabbagh Realty, known simply as KSR, represented the seller in the transaction. The two commercial properties — one seven-story property and an adjacent three-story, late-19th-century building — were only on the market for about two months with competing offers until the sellers settled on a cash offer from Zar, according to Sultan. “With all the AI and tech tenants that are propping up the market in terms of leasing, the companies want to be centered around Downtown and live-work-play submarkets like SoHo and NoHo,” Sultan told CO. “I think that is a testament to why this building had as much interest; we had three or four buyers all competing for this.” But Zar did not waste any time, closing the deal within 30 days. Current tenants at the NoHo properties include art gallery Aicon Contemporary. Just across the street at 375 Lafayette Street, Minskoff Equities and Edison Properties are constructing two 99-unit multifamily properties where a parking lot currently sits. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Zar Properties acquires two NoHo mixed-use buildings at 31-35 Great Jones Street, Manhattan for $21M from Scott family (50+ year ownership).
Seven-story and three-story late-19th-century loft buildings; high ceilings, flexible layouts positioned for upscale office and potential residential conversion.
Zar targeting NoHo loft character and mixed-use potential amid competitive office, retail, residential market.
stories.summary: Zar Properties purchased two adjacent mixed-use buildings at 31-35 Great Jones Street in Manhattan's NoHo neighborhood for $21 million from the Scott family of Great Jones Realty, which held the properties for at least five decades. The buildings comprise a seven-story tower and a three-story late-19th-century structure with loft-style spaces, high ceilings, and flexible layouts. Zar plans to position the properties for upscale office and mixed-use tenancy.
stories.impact: Moderate signal for Manhattan multifamily: Zar's acquisition of loft-style NoHo buildings at $21M (basis unclear on SF) suggests developer confidence in NoHo conversion/repositioning potential (office-to-residential conversion, mixed-use). NoHo is a constrained-supply submarket with strong renter demand (young professionals, creative class). If Zar converts to residential, this adds modest supply but validates that NoHo fundamentals support premium-priced conversion projects. Conversely, continued office/mixed-use positioning indicates office recovery narrative in prime Manhattan neighborhoods; neither scenario materially increases multifamily supply, but validates neighborhood strength and likely rent resilience in nearby multifamily assets.

stories.title: MNRK Music Group Inks 8K SF at Rosen’s 443 Park Avenue South
stories.excerpt: Independent music company MNRK Music Group has leased 7,629 square feet at the Rosen family’s 443 Park Avenue South office building, Commercial Observer has learned. The seven-year, seven-month office lease occupies the entire ninth floor of the 11-story tower, according to Koeppel Rosen, the leasing and management agent for the Rosen family portfolio. The building is at the corner of Park Avenue and East 30th Street near Manhattan’s Murray Hill neighborhood. Koeppel Rosen’s Max Koeppel handled the deal in-house for the landlord. Transwestern’s Luke Dillmeier, Patrick Heeg and Thomas Hines negotiated on behalf of MNRK Music in the transaction. The asking rent was $48 per square foot, according to a source familiar with the deal. MNRK Music, which manages a portfolio of labels and acts that includes Last Gang Records and folk band The Lumineers, currently lists its New York offices at the Trump Organization’s 40 Wall Street. The group moved into 443 Park Avenue South in mid-July, according to a source. It is unclear whether the move marks a relocation or an expansion for MNRK Music. Other tenants at the Midtown South building include cloud data firm Ardoq, software firm LMI and architecture firm David Smotrich & Partners. Its retail component is occupied by a Joe Coffee Company location, as well as a storefront for apparel and footwear retailer Comme Des Garcons. Spokespeople for MNRK Music Group and Transwestern did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: MNRK Music Group leases 7,629 SF, entire ninth floor at 443 Park Avenue South, Manhattan (Park Ave + East 30th, Murray Hill).
Seven-year, seven-month lease at $48/SF; moved from Trump Organization's 40 Wall Street; mid-July move date.
MNRK Music (Last Gang Records, The Lumineers label portfolio) expansion/relocation signals creative/media sector office demand in Manhattan East Midtown.
stories.summary: MNRK Music Group, an independent music company managing labels and acts including Last Gang Records and folk band The Lumineers, leased 7,629 square feet (the entire ninth floor) at 443 Park Avenue South in Manhattan's Murray Hill neighborhood. The seven-year, seven-month lease was struck at $48 per square foot. The company relocated from the Trump Organization's 40 Wall Street in mid-July; it is unclear whether the move represents expansion or relocation.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance. However, creative/media sector office leasing in East Midtown (Park Ave South, Murray Hill) signals ongoing white-collar demand recovery in secondary Manhattan submarkets beyond Hudson Yards and SoHo. Music/media tenants typically correlate with younger workforce demographics and higher renter density in nearby residential; this supports demand fundamentals for adjacent or nearby multifamily assets in Murray Hill and Gramercy. No supply implication; primarily a secondary demand signal.

stories.title: ESRT Selling 1359 Broadway to Thor for $218M
stories.excerpt: Only a month after Commercial Observer learned it was going on the market, Empire State Realty Trust (ESRT) has found a buyer for 1359 Broadway in Thor Equities, which agreed to pay $218 million for the 22-story office building, according to sources. This is not much lower than the $225 million the 486,000-square-foot property was being shopped around for earlier this summer. Neither ESRT nor Thor responded to CO’s requests for comment. ESRT was represented by Newmark’s Adam Spies, Josh King, Adam Doneger, Avery Silverstein, Marcella Fasulo and Doug Harmon, who also did not respond to requests for comment by press time. CO was not able to learn who represented Thor. The property, just two blocks north of Herald Square, was 95 percent occupied as of last month, having inked recent leases with Infinium Wall Systems, SLCE Architects and nonprofit Braven, and has a Wolfgang’s Steakhouse and Wokuni in the retail portion. The purchase, expected to close in the next month or two and not official yet, is not Thor’s first dip into the Midtown office market this year. In March, CO reported that Joe Sitt’s company had purchased Michael Haddad’s 58,000-square-foot office and retail building, 1165 Broadway, for $56 million. Max Gross can be reached at mgross@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Empire State Realty Trust sells 1359 Broadway (486,000 SF, 22-story office tower) to Thor Equities for $218M; one month after listing.
Property 95% leased, two blocks north of Herald Square; recent tenant additions include Infinium Wall Systems, SLCE Architects, Braven nonprofit.
Sale price near asking ($225M asking); closing expected within one to two months; reflects Manhattan office distress and repricing.
stories.summary: Empire State Realty Trust (ESRT) sold 1359 Broadway, a 486,000-square-foot, 22-story office tower in Manhattan, to Thor Equities for $218 million. The sale occurred approximately one month after the property hit the market at $225 million asking. The building was 95 percent occupied at the time of sale, with recent leases signed by Infinium Wall Systems, SLCE Architects, and nonprofit Braven. A Wolfgang's Steakhouse and Wokuni occupy the retail floors.
stories.impact: Manhattan office distress indicator with secondary multifamily implications: ESRT's willingness to sell a 95%-leased building near asking (only 3% haircut) signals that opportunistic capital (Thor) is comfortable acquiring stabilized Manhattan office at current valuations, likely betting on long-term office recovery or mixed-use conversion potential (Herald Square is a high-foot-traffic, mixed-use neighborhood). For multifamily developers, this affirms that Manhattan office towers near mass transit and retail corridors (Herald Square, 34th St subway hub) retain acquisition interest and could be conversion candidates; however, no immediate supply relief expected. Continued office sales in this range suggest cap rates remain pressure points for new multifamily construction financing; money flowing to stabilized office deals may reduce debt availability and raise multifamily construction loan rates in the tri-state.

stories.title: Finmarc Buys NoVA Office Complex for $78M
stories.excerpt: Finmarc Management has acquired a pair of office towers in Tysons, Va., for $77.5 million as the company begins another wave of acquisitions while doubling down on office space in Northern Virginia. The Bethesda, Md.-based investment firm acquired Highline at Greensboro from CIM Group. The two 10-story Class A buildings at 8401 and 8405 Greensboro Drive total roughly 460,000 square feet and were 70 percent leased at the time of the sale. “We remain buyers of office buildings and other assets in the greater DMV market, especially Northern Virginia because of our continued confidence in the regional market fundamentals,” Finmarc Principal Neil Markus said in a statement. Highline at Greensboro is near The Boro mixed-use complex and the Greensboro Metro station. The property features a fitness center, a golf simulator and a day care. Over the past two years, new tenants Mortgage One Solutions signed for 23,108 square feet and Tegna took 23,016 square feet. Cushman & Wakefield’s Paul Collins and Kevin Sidney represented CIM. Metropolis Capital Advisors’ Cliff Mendelson assisted Finmarc with the debt placement. Cushman & Wakefield’s Josh Masi and Paige Barger handle leasing at the Highline at Greensboro. Finmarc has been betting on discounted Northern Virginia offices. The company paid $51 million late last year for the nearly 620,000-square-foot Dulles Corner portfolio after acquiring the roughly 500,000-square-foot Trinity Centre for nearly $40 million the previous summer. The company funded the Highline acquisition partly with proceeds from three dispositions completed over the past six weeks, including office/flex and retail assets in Virginia and North Carolina. Finmarc also said it has more dry powder coming from expected sales over the next two to three months, and plans to reinvest the proceeds into another $250 million to $300 million of acquisitions. The firm currently owns and manages nearly 7.5 million square feet across the Mid-Atlantic. Gregory Corn
bullets: Finmarc Management acquires Highline at Greensboro office complex, Tysons Corner, Northern Virginia for $77.5M from CIM Group.
Two 10-story Class A buildings, 460,000 SF total, 70% leased at sale; recent tenants: Mortgage One Solutions (23,108 SF), Tegna (23,016 SF).
Finmarc focuses on Northern Virginia office acquisitions; targets DMV market fundamentals and Greensboro's proximity to Metro station and The Boro mixed-use.
stories.summary: Finmarc Management acquired the Highline at Greensboro office complex in Tysons, Virginia from CIM Group for $77.5 million. The property comprises two 10-story Class A buildings totaling approximately 460,000 square feet and was 70 percent leased at sale. Recent tenants include Mortgage One Solutions (23,108 SF) and Tegna (23,016 SF). The buildings feature amenities including a fitness center, golf simulator, and day care. Finmarc affirmed its bullish stance on Northern Virginia office and broader DMV market fundamentals.
stories.impact: IMPORTANT SIGNAL for multifamily in Northern Virginia: Finmarc's acquisition of 70%-leased Tysons office at $77.5M ($169/SF on operating basis) signals developer confidence in Northern Virginia office recovery and corporate tenant stability (Mortgage One Solutions, Tegna—financial services, media tech). Office stabilization near Greensboro Metro station and The Boro mixed-use suggests sustained foot traffic, transit ridership, and ecosystem demand that supports multifamily leasing in Tysons, Reston, Arlington corridors. However, at 70% occupancy, the property remains below pre-pandemic stabilization norms, indicating Northern Virginia office market has not fully recovered; this may constrain wage growth and job-seeker in-migration, tempering multifamily rent growth assumptions. Developers should monitor Tysons/Reston submarket absorption closely: if Finmarc can stabilize to 85%+ occupancy and attract Class-A tenants, multifamily rent growth will follow 12–18 months later. Finmarc's repeated capital deployment in NoVA suggests continued conviction; multifamily developers should model Northern Virginia as a sustained growth corridor but remain cautious on near-term rent acceleration.
